questions.stem: Explain how you would implement a level-order traversal of a binary tree using a queue.
markingGuide: Initialize an empty queue and enqueue the root node.
While the queue is not empty, dequeue a node and visit it.
Enqueue the left and right children of the visited node if they exist.
Continue until the queue is empty.
questions.explanation: Level-order traversal requires visiting nodes level by level. Using a queue allows us to process nodes in the order they are encountered, ensuring each level is fully processed before moving to the next.

questions.stem: Describe the process of converting a recursive in-order traversal of a binary tree to an iterative version using an explicit stack.
markingGuide: Initialize an empty stack and set a pointer to the root node.
While the pointer is not null or the stack is not empty, repeat the following:
Push the current node onto the stack and move the pointer to the left child.
If the pointer is null, pop a node from the stack, visit it, and set the pointer to its right child.
Continue until both the pointer is null and the stack is empty.
questions.explanation: Converting recursive to iterative involves simulating the call stack with an explicit stack. This approach maintains the order of node visits as in the recursive method.
